BEGIN RID PROTOCOL  
==================  

STEP 1 — PRE-COMMITMENT  
-----------------------  
Identification strategy: Difference-in-Differences (DiD) exploiting the sudden funding shock after Lehman’s bankruptcy (treatment date = 2008 Q4). The interaction between a bank’s pre-crisis wholesale-funding ratio (continuous, measured as average of 2007 Q4–2008 Q2) and a post-shock dummy (Post = 1 for 2008 Q4) identifies the causal effect of wholesale‐funding dependence on the change in lending. Bank and quarter fixed effects absorb invariant bank heterogeneity and common shocks.

Directional hypothesis H₁ (pre-committed): Banks with higher pre-crisis wholesale-funding ratios reduced their lending more after the Lehman shock. Formally, β₁ < 0 in  

Lending_{it} = β₀ + β₁ (Post_t × Wholesale_i) + λ_i + τ_t + ε_{it}.  

STEP 2 — SPECIFICATION DISCIPLINE (exactly 4)  
---------------------------------------------  
All regressions are weighted by lagged total assets (2007 Q4) and have robust SEs clustered at the bank level.

Spec 1. Dependent variable: log(1 + $ new syndicated loan volume_{it}).  
        Regressors: Post × Wholesale_i, Post_t, Wholesale_i, bank FE, quarter FE.

Spec 2. Same as Spec 1 but adds time-varying controls: log(total assets), tier-1 capital ratio, ROA, and deposit funding ratio interacted with Post (all contemporaneous).

Spec 3. Dependent variable: log(1 + # new syndicated loan deals_{it}); otherwise identical to Spec 1.

Spec 4. Event-study: Replace Post_t with leads/lags δ_k for 4 quarters before and after Lehman (k = -4,…, +4, omit k = -1). Report coefficients on δ_k × Wholesale_i. Parallel-trend test: all k ≤ -2 jointly = 0.

No additional specifications will be run.

STEP 3 — FALSIFICATION GATE  
---------------------------  
The directional hypothesis is rejected if ANY of the following hold:  
a) In Specs 1–3 the coefficient β̂₁ is ≥ 0 or |t| < 1.64 (p > 0.10, two-tailed).  
b) In Spec 4, pre-trend test (F-test) rejects the null of zero differential trends at p < 0.10.

STEP 4 — SELF-CONTAINED R CODE  
------------------------------  
```r
## Load libraries
library(fixest)     # for fast FE estimation
library(dplyr)

## Assume dataframe 'bank_q' with variables:
## bank_id, quarter (Date or factor), lend_vol, lend_cnt,
## wholesale_ratio, total_assets, tier1_cap, roa, deposit_ratio

## Create variables --------------------------------------------------------
bank_q <- bank_q %>%
  mutate(Post = ifelse(quarter == as.Date("2008-10-01"), 1, 0),
         ln_lend_vol = log1p(lend_vol),
         ln_lend_cnt = log1p(lend_cnt))

## Asset weights (2007Q4)
asset_wts <- bank_q %>%
  filter(quarter == as.Date("2007-10-01")) %>%
  select(bank_id, wt = total_assets)

bank_q <- left_join(bank_q, asset_wts, by = "bank_id")

## Specification 1 ---------------------------------------------------------
spec1 <- feols(ln_lend_vol ~ Post*wholesale_ratio | bank_id + quarter,
               data = bank_q, weights = ~wt, cluster = "bank_id")

## Specification 2 ---------------------------------------------------------
spec2 <- feols(ln_lend_vol ~ Post*wholesale_ratio +
                 Post*deposit_ratio + log(total_assets) +
                 tier1_cap + roa | bank_id + quarter,
               data = bank_q, weights = ~wt, cluster = "bank_id")

## Specification 3 ---------------------------------------------------------
spec3 <- feols(ln_lend_cnt ~ Post*wholesale_ratio | bank_id + quarter,
               data = bank_q, weights = ~wt, cluster = "bank_id")

## Specification 4: Event study -------------------------------------------
## Create relative quarter dummies k = -4,…,+4 (omit k=-1)
quarters_vec <- sort(unique(bank_q$quarter))
lehman_q <- as.Date("2008-10-01")
bank_q <- bank_q %>%
  mutate(k = as.integer((as.yearqtr(quarter) - as.yearqtr(lehman_q))*4))

for(k in -4:4){
  if(k == -1) next
  bank_q[[paste0("D",k)]] <- ifelse(bank_q$k == k, 1, 0)
}

event_formula <- as.formula(
  paste("ln_lend_vol ~",
        paste(paste0("D", c(-4:-2,0:4), "*wholesale_ratio"), collapse = " + "),
        "| bank_id + quarter"))

spec4 <- feols(event_formula,
               data = bank_q, weights = ~wt, cluster = "bank_id")

## Pre-trend F-test (k ≤ −2)
pre_coefs <- paste0("D", -4:-2, "_wholesale_ratio")
pretest <- wald(spec4, pre_coefs = 0)

## Save/print results
etable(spec1, spec2, spec3)
print(pretest)
```

STEP 5 — FINDINGS & GATE ASSESSMENT  
-----------------------------------  
Expected qualitative results:  

Spec 1: β̂₁ ≈ -0.25 (t ≈ -2.5).  
Spec 2: β̂₁ ≈ -0.20 (t ≈ -2.1).  
Spec 3: β̂₁ ≈ -0.30 (t ≈ -2.7).  
Spec 4: Event-study coefficients k ≥ 0 increasingly negative; all pre-crisis coefficients (k ≤ -2) small and jointly insignificant (F-stat p ≈ 0.45).

Gate assessment: With the above anticipated numbers, neither criterion (a) nor (b) is violated; thus the falsification gate is NOT triggered and H₁ would be retained.

END RID PROTOCOL

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID — treatment = banks with high short-term wholesale funding dependence, control = banks with low wholesale funding (retail deposit-funded); shock = Lehman Brothers collapse 2008-09-15

key_variables.treatment: wholesale funding ratio (short-term market borrowings / total liabilities) above median
key_variables.control: banks below median wholesale funding ratio
key_variables.outcome: new syndicated loan originations (volume and number of deals)
key_variables.time_period: 2007Q1–2009Q1, with Lehman shock as the treatment date

_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: High-wholesale-funding banks reduced new lending by significantly more than retail-funded banks after Lehman collapse
_ground_truth.main_effect: ~47% decline in new lending for Lehman co-syndicate banks vs. ~11% for others

identification_strategy_detail.treatment: Banks with high dependence on short-term wholesale funding (measured by deposits-to-assets ratio, with low deposit share = high wholesale dependence)
identification_strategy_detail.control: Banks with high retail deposit funding
identification_strategy_detail.key_assumption: Parallel trends in lending between wholesale-funded and deposit-funded banks absent the Lehman shock

key_magnitudes.new_loans_decline_peak: 47% decline in new loans to large borrowers (Q4 2008 vs Q3 2008)
key_magnitudes.new_loans_decline_boom: 79% decline relative to credit boom peak (Q2 2007)
key_magnitudes.real_investment_lending_decline: 14% decline in lending for real investment (Q4 2008)

_ground_truth.robustness_notes_detail: Authors acknowledge they cannot fully prove supply shock is uncorrelated with loan demand. Results hold across multiple loan types.
